b: Learn how to install NovelForge on Windows 10 or 11, start it for the first time and create your first novel. There is no installer: you install Python once, unzip a folder and double-click one file. What you need Windows 10 or 11. NovelForge has only been built and tested on Windows. macOS and Linux are not supported. Python 3.13 or newer. It is a free program from python.org that NovelForge runs on. Two small Python libraries, python-docx (it reads and writes the Word files) and Pillow (it draws the map images). Write.bat installs them for you the first time; that is the only time NovelForge needs the internet. Install Python Download Python from python.org , choose version 3.13 or newer, and on the first screen of the installer tick Add python.exe to PATH . b: Every keyboard shortcut in NovelForge's main window, by menu. This page is generated from the program's own source code each time the website is built, so it lists exactly the keys the menus show, and it cannot fall behind the program. You do not have to remember any of them. Press Ctrl + Shift + P to open the command palette, type a few letters of what you want ( story graph , backup , theme ) and press Enter. It searches every command in every menu. How undo and redo behave Undo has two jobs, and which one you get depends on where the cursor is. With the cursor inside the writing area, Ctrl + Z undoes your typing . Anywhere else, it undoes the last change to the project: a rename, a move, a delete, an edit in the inspector. b: Learn how to find, add, rename, reorder and delete things in the binder, the tree on the left of the main window. Most rows are real files or folders on your disk (outline beats and timeline events live in the small project.json file instead), and every delete can be undone. What the binder shows The top level of the tree has twelve groups, always in this order: Manuscript, Outline & Beats, Characters, Locations, Items, Factions, Plot Threads, World Bible, Maps, Timeline, Notes & Research and Publishing. A number on the right of each row tells you what is inside it: Manuscript shows the word count of the whole book. Under it are your chapters, each with its word count, and under each chapter its scenes, each with theirs. A novel with three chapters or fewer opens with every chapter expanded. d: Learn how NovelForge protects your novel: verified zip backups, per-document versions, safe saving and the recovery journal, and how to restore an older copy.
h: The layers that protect your writing
b: Learn how NovelForge keeps your novel safe and how to bring an older copy back. Two separate features do the work, because they fail in different ways: backups copy the whole project, and versions keep earlier copies of a single document. The layers that protect your writing Safe saving. Every document is written to a temporary file, checked to be a valid Word file, and only then swapped in for the real one, so a crash in the middle of a save leaves the previous version untouched. A sync program such as OneDrive therefore sees either the old file or the new one, never a half-written one. Autosave writes the scene you are typing in thirty seconds after you stop typing. The recovery journal records your typing a second and a half after you pause. If the power goes out, the next start offers the words back and puts the cursor where you left it. Your questions, answered Short, honest answers about price, privacy, files, platforms, importing your work, and what NovelForge can and cannot do. What is NovelForge? NovelForge is free, open-source novel writing software for Windows. It combines a binder of chapters and scenes, a corkboard, nine outline frameworks, a timeline, reference sheets for characters and places, a story graph that checks continuity, a procedural fantasy map maker and offline prose diagnostics. Every scene it creates is a real Microsoft Word (.docx) file in a folder on your own disk. Is NovelForge really free? Yes. It is released under the MIT licence: free to use, copy, change and share. b: Home Support Support the project NovelForge is free, and always will be No subscription, no paywalled feature, no account. If it is useful to you, a donation is welcome but never expected. There are other ways to help that cost nothing. Say thank you Scan a code or follow a link. Every contribution helps keep NovelForge free. PayPal paypal.me/OmAbhyankar UPI (India) abhyankarom10@ybl Other ways to help Tell a writer. The most useful thing you can do is mention NovelForge to someone who is trying to finish a book. Star the project on GitHub ; it helps other writers find it. Report what feels wrong. “It felt glitchy when I did this” is a complete bug report. Open an issue . Ask for what you need. If Mac or Linux support, a new outline framework or a new map style would change how you write, say so. Contribute. Code, tests, documentation and name lists are all welcome; see CONTRIBUTING.md .
